rv.q: It shows off Harris's impressive poetic muscles, but it also bends out of true, warping a little from what she asks it to contain.
Harris sets each piece — delicately and ruthlessly — in its proper place, until a giant mosaic of contradictions comes screaming into focus.
On Sugarland feels both overstuffed and underwritten.
Whitney White's direction of his actors is masterful.
Harris spins a circular narrative, one that often loops back on itself like the cul-de-sac where it's set.
So much of On Sugarland does get out of hand, some of it for reasons germane to the script, but too often for reasons undercutting the script.
